lead.label: 4de
lead.why: Abstract: 'compounds 4de (EC50 = 0.23 ug/mL) and 4dq (EC50 = 0.11 ug/mL) displayed the best efficacy'; 4de is named first and is the one taken to in vivo curative tests against Fg ('compound 4de ... in vivo curative activities').

reactions.conditions: Pictet-Spengler: conc. H2SO4 (0.5 mL), water, rt, overnight (12 h); product precipitates, filtered; 95%.
reactions.source: main text, Results/Chemistry and Experimental, 'Synthesis of Compound 1'; Scheme 2 step a

reactions.conditions: CuBr2 (0.2 equiv), DBU (2 equiv), MeCN, air, rt, 2.5 h; yellow solid filtered; 92%.
reactions.source: main text Experimental, 'Synthesis of Compound 2'; Scheme 2 step b

reactions.conditions: NH3.H2O (aq. ammonium hydroxide), MeOH, reflux, 24 h; pH adjusted to 8 with 1 M HCl; 85%.
reactions.source: main text Experimental, 'Synthesis of Compound 3'; Scheme 2 step c

reactions.conditions: PyBOP (1 equiv), Et3N (8 equiv), CH2Cl2, rt, overnight; product precipitates; 88%.
reactions.source: main text Experimental, general procedure for 3da-3dp and 4da-4fj and entry 4de; Scheme 2 step d

notes: Abstract names two best compounds (4de and 4dq, both made by the same 4-step route, differing only in the hydrazine); 4de chosen as it is also the in vivo compound. Compound 1 has no printed name; structure derived from the text (Pictet-Spengler of Trp-OMe with glyoxylic acid, then 1-carboxylic acid / 3-methyl ester, consistent with product 2 name); stereochemistry omitted (not stated, C1 centre not defined). The substituted hydrazine (4-fluorophenylhydrazine) is not named explicitly in the general procedure; inferred from the product name 4de (4-fluorophenyl on the hydrazide NH). Reagents are described as purchased (analytical grade supplier) in the general statement; no hydrazine supplier is given individually. Printed HRMS formula for 3 (C13H13N2O4) is a typo in the paper; irrelevant to the structure.
